claims.claim: A well-planned vegan diet can be health-promoting for healthy adults, with B12 supplementation and sufficient nutrients.
claims.source_check: Accessible original publisher pages, abstracts, institutional statements and/or secondary analyses compared; see per-source check details
claims.limitations: Not every vegan diet is automatically healthy; evidence and recommendations differ for vulnerable groups.

claims.claim: Reliable vitamin B12 intake is necessary for vegan diets; unfortified plants are not dependable natural sources.
claims.source_check: Accessible original publisher pages, abstracts, institutional statements and/or secondary analyses compared; see per-source check details
claims.limitations: Supplementation schedules and lab interpretation depend on the individual; no dose is prescribed here.

claims.claim: In one small resistance-training study, protein-matched high-protein vegan and omnivorous diets supported similar gains in untrained young men.
claims.source_check: Accessible original publisher pages, abstracts, institutional statements and/or secondary analyses compared; see per-source check details
claims.limitations: Small n=38, young men only, protein matched at ~1.6 g/kg/day with supplements; findings cannot be generalised to all diets, ages or athletes.

claims.claim: In a modelled UK-group comparison, vegan diets had 25.1% of high-meat diets' greenhouse-gas emissions, with a 95% uncertainty interval of 15.1–37.0%.
claims.source_check: Accessible original publisher pages, abstracts, institutional statements and/or secondary analyses compared; see per-source check details
claims.limitations: Modelled group averages in a UK cohort; not a person's carbon footprint, causal intervention or a worldwide constant.

claims.claim: OWID reports that 77% of global soy (2018 allocation) was used as feed for livestock; 7% was directly eaten as tofu, soy milk and similar foods.
claims.source_check: Accessible original publisher pages, abstracts, institutional statements and/or secondary analyses compared; see per-source check details
claims.limitations: Secondary synthesis using historical commodity allocation; an individual tofu's supply chain still needs tracing.

claims.claim: A plant-based label does not guarantee health; nutritional quality and processing both matter, supported by public guidance and observational cohort research.
claims.source_check: Accessible original publisher pages, abstracts, institutional statements and/or secondary analyses compared; see per-source check details
claims.limitations: Observational associations are not proof that processing alone causes disease. Not all processed products are unhealthy.

claims.claim: DGE 2024 neither universally recommends nor opposes vegan diets for children, pregnancy, breastfeeding, adolescents and older adults, due to limited evidence and higher consequences of inadequacy.
claims.source_check: Accessible original publisher pages, abstracts, institutional statements and/or secondary analyses compared; see per-source check details
claims.limitations: Specialist care, energy sufficiency and individual nutrients are essential; this is not an individual health recommendation.

claims.claim: Animal consciousness has strong scientific support for mammals and birds; deciding what welfare and moral status require is an ethical rather than purely empirical question.
claims.source_check: Accessible original publisher pages, abstracts, institutional statements and/or secondary analyses compared; see per-source check details
claims.limitations: The New York Declaration is an expert statement, not a moral consensus or proof that all species experience life alike.

claims.claim: Animals are harmed during crop production, but published analysis notes that robust total counts and simple diet-level comparisons are not currently established.
claims.source_check: Accessible original publisher pages, abstracts, institutional statements and/or secondary analyses compared; see per-source check details
claims.limitations: No reliable universal vegan-versus-omnivorous animal-death count; ethical comparisons depend on the species, effects and farming context.

claims.claim: A 150-country modelling study found nutritious sustainable dietary patterns often cost less in high-income countries but more in lower-income countries; access is context-dependent.
claims.source_check: Accessible original publisher pages, abstracts, institutional statements and/or secondary analyses compared; see per-source check details
claims.limitations: Modelled 2017 average food-price data, not real-time supermarket prices, and not proof that every vegan diet or household is cheaper.

limitations: A citation alone is not proof; this register records the scope of checks actually performed. Ethical conclusions cannot be assigned a purely scientific confidence score.
